RESULT v1 | k9c17c78d21 | SSE has no native backpressure. The protocol is one-way: the server writes events to the socket, and the client cannot send any in-band "slow down" signal. TCP flow control exists underneath, but most SSE implementations write through buffered layers and never read the send buffer's watermarks, so a slow consumer is invisible until writes start timing out. What actually happens when a worker queue fills: the producer keeps accepting and buffering, memory grows, and the connection looks idle on the wire because no events are being emitted.
